title: Lump Sum vs Dollar-Cost Averaging: Which Wins More?
description:
Lump sum vs dollar-cost averaging: if you already have the cash, investing it all at once has beaten spreading it out about two-thirds of the time (68% in Vanguard's study of global stocks, 1976–2022), because stocks usually beat cash. Spreading it out still beat sitting in cash 69% of the time, and it can make a drop easier to live with.

Sources:
- Vanguard, Finlay & Zorn, "Cost averaging: Invest now or temporarily hold your cash?", February 2023 (MSCI World Index returns 1976–2022, 100% stocks, lump sum vs. three equal monthly parts, compared after one year): https://corporate.vanguard.com/content/dam/corp/research/pdf/cost_averaging_invest_now_or_temporarily_hold_your_cash.pdf

Example assumptions: $12,000 invested at once vs. $1,000 at the start of each month for 12 months, a steady 7% yearly return, uninvested cash earns nothing, no fees or taxes. Real markets don't move steadily; returns vary, can be negative, and past results don't guarantee future returns. Not financial advice.

es.summary: Según Vanguard (acciones globales, 1976–2022), invertir todo de una vez ganó a repartirlo el 68% de las veces. Pero repartirlo superó al efectivo el 69%.

pt.title: Tudo de uma vez ou todo mês: o que rende mais?
pt.summary: Segundo a Vanguard (ações globais, 1976–2022), investir tudo de uma vez venceu o aporte parcelado em 68% das vezes. Mas parcelar venceu o dinheiro parado em 69%.

scenes.say: You have twelve thousand dollars to invest. All at once, or a thousand a month? History has a favorite.
Vanguard studied global stocks from nineteen seventy-six to twenty twenty-two. Investing all at once beat spreading it out about two-thirds of the time.

visual.label: of the time, lump sum won

scenes.say: Why? Stocks usually beat cash. So money waiting on the sidelines usually missed growth.
In a steady seven percent year, all at once ends about three hundred ninety dollars ahead.
But if the market drops right after you invest, spreading it out wins. And it still beat leaving the money in cash sixty-nine percent of the time.

visual.label: of the time, spreading it out beat cash

scenes.say: So if fear of a crash would keep you in cash, investing in steps beats waiting. And if you invest from each paycheck, keep going. That's investing as soon as you can.
Follow for one money lesson every day.
